title: OSHA general industry fire protection practice questions
description: Free OSHA general industry fire protection practice questions on 29 CFR 1910 Subpart L. Every answer is explained and linked to its section.

questions.question: Under 1910.155(b), Subpart L applies to all employments apart from which ones?
questions.explanation: "This subpart applies to all employments except for maritime, construction, and agriculture."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.155, Scope, application and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Subpart L definitions, a fire involving flammable or combustible liquids, flammable gases and greases is which class of fire?
questions.explanation: "Class B fire means a fire involving flammable or combustible liquids, flammable gases, greases and similar materials, and some rubber and plastic materials."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.155, Scope, application and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How does 1910.155 define an incipient stage fire?

options.A: Any fire inside a building or enclosed structure
options.B: A fire that has spread beyond the room where it started
options.C: A fire that only a fire brigade may fight
options.D: A fire in its initial or beginning stage that can be controlled or extinguished by portable fire extinguishers, Class II standpipe or small hose systems without protective clothing or breathing apparatus

questions.explanation: An incipient stage fire is "a fire which is in the initial or beginning stage and which can be controlled or extinguished by portable fire extinguishers, Class II standpipe or small hose systems without the need for protective clothing or breathing apparatus."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.155, Scope, application and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under the Subpart L definitions, what makes maintenance different from inspection?

options.A: Maintenance is done only by the manufacturer
options.B: Maintenance requires the checking of internal fittings, devices and agent supplies
options.C: Maintenance is only a visual check that equipment is in place
options.D: Maintenance is needed only after an extinguisher has been used

questions.explanation: Inspection is "a visual check" that equipment is in place, charged and ready, while "Maintenance differs from inspection in that maintenance requires the checking of internal fittings, devices and agent supplies."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.155, Scope, application and definitions applicable to this subpart (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.157(c)(3), portable fire extinguishers using which extinguishing agents may the employer not provide or make available in the workplace?
questions.explanation: "The employer shall not provide or make available in the workplace portable fire extinguishers using carbon tetrachloride or chlorobromomethane extinguishing agents."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: In what condition must the employer keep portable fire extinguishers, and where?

options.A: Partly charged, in a locked storeroom
options.B: Empty, until a fire is reported
options.C: Fully charged during working hours only, in any convenient place
options.D: Fully charged and operable, in their designated places at all times except during use

questions.explanation: "The employer shall assure that portable fire extinguishers are maintained in a fully charged and operable condition and kept in their designated places at all times except during use."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For portable fire extinguishers provided for employee use on Class A fires, what is the maximum travel distance for employees to any extinguisher?
questions.explanation: Extinguishers for Class A fires must be distributed "so that the travel distance for employees to any extinguisher is 75 feet (22.9 m) or less."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For portable fire extinguishers provided for employee use on Class B fires, what is the maximum travel distance from the Class B hazard area to any extinguisher?
questions.explanation: Class B extinguishers must be distributed "so that the travel distance from the Class B hazard area to any extinguisher is 50 feet (15.2 m) or less."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Portable fire extinguishers for Class D hazards are required in combustible metal working areas where combustible metal powders, flakes or shavings are generated how often?

options.B: At least once every six months
options.D: At least once every two weeks

questions.explanation: Class D extinguishers "are required in those combustible metal working areas where combustible metal powders, flakes, shavings, or similarly sized products are generated at least once every two weeks."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: On what basis does 1910.157(d)(5) say extinguishers used for Class C hazards are distributed?

options.A: The appropriate pattern for the existing Class A or Class B hazards
options.C: A fixed travel distance of 25 feet
options.D: The number of employees on each shift

questions.explanation: "The employer shall distribute portable fire extinguishers used for Class C hazards on the basis of the appropriate pattern for the existing Class A or Class B hazards."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How often must portable extinguishers (or hose used in lieu of them under 1910.157(d)(3)) be visually inspected?
questions.explanation: "Portable extinguishers or hose used in lieu thereof under paragraph (d)(3) of this section shall be visually inspected monthly."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How long must the employer retain the record of a portable extinguisher's annual maintenance date?

options.C: One year after the last entry or the life of the shell, whichever is less
options.D: Only until the extinguisher is recharged

questions.explanation: The employer must "record the annual maintenance date and retain this record for one year after the last entry or the life of the shell, whichever is less."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Stored pressure dry chemical extinguishers that require a 12-year hydrostatic test must be emptied and subjected to applicable maintenance procedures how often?
questions.explanation: These extinguishers must be "emptied and subjected to applicable maintenance procedures every 6 years"; extinguishers with non-refillable disposable containers are exempt, and the 6 years restart from the date of recharging or hydrostatic testing.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.157(f)(10), how often must carbon dioxide extinguishers be hydrostatically tested?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide extinguishers and nitrogen or carbon dioxide cylinders used with wheeled extinguishers must be "tested every 5 years at 5/3 of the service pressure as stamped into the cylinder."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: At what pressure must dry chemical and dry powder hose assemblies with a shut-off nozzle be hydrostatically tested?
questions.explanation: "The employer shall assure that dry chemical and dry powder hose assemblies with a shut-off nozzle are hydrostatically tested at 300 psi (2,070 kPa)." The 1,250 psi figure is for carbon dioxide hose assemblies.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Where portable fire extinguishers are provided for employee use, when must the employer provide the educational program on extinguisher use and incipient stage fire fighting hazards?

options.A: Only after a fire has occurred
options.B: Upon initial employment and at least annually thereafter
options.C: Once, when the extinguishers are first installed

questions.explanation: "The employer shall provide the education required in paragraph (g)(1) of this section upon initial employment and at least annually thereafter."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.157, Portable fire extinguishers (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an automatic sprinkler system installed to comply with 1910.159, how often must a main drain flow test be performed on each system?

options.B: Only when the system is first installed

questions.explanation: "The employer shall assure that a main drain flow test is performed on each system annually." The inspector's test valve must be opened "at least every two years."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.159, Automatic sprinkler systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: Under 1910.164(e)(3), for how long at most may the employer delay alarms or devices initiated by fire detector actuation, unless a longer delay is necessary for the immediate safety of employees?
questions.explanation: "The employer shall not delay alarms or devices initiated by fire detector actuation for more than 30 seconds unless such delay is necessary for the immediate safety of employees." Such a delay must be addressed in an emergency action plan meeting 1910.38.

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.164, Fire detection systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: How often must the reliability and adequacy of non-supervised employee alarm systems be tested?

options.D: Only after the system is repaired

questions.explanation: "The employer shall assure that a test of the reliability and adequacy of non-supervised employee alarm systems is made every two months." Supervised systems are tested "at least annually."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.165, Employee alarm systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)

questions.question: For an employer with 10 or fewer employees in a particular workplace, what does 1910.165(b)(5) accept as a procedure for sounding the alarm?

options.A: Sending an e-mail to each employee
options.B: Direct voice communication, provided all employees can hear the alarm
options.C: Posting a written notice after the emergency
options.D: Calling the local fire department only

questions.explanation: "For those employers with 10 or fewer employees in a particular workplace, direct voice communication is an acceptable procedure for sounding the alarm provided all employees can hear the alarm. Such workplaces need not have a back-up system."

source.title: eCFR: 29 CFR 1910.165, Employee alarm systems (as of Nov 3, 2026)
